sentences.text: A clinical trial has been launched in the UK which scientists hope could cut years from the search for new treatments for Alzheimer's disease.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: It will test multiple drugs simultaneously, starting with two repurposed medicines already used to treat type 2 diabetes and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: The study will examine whether the drugs can lessen symptoms such as memory and thinking problems, and help people maintain their quality of life.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Angela Bucksey, 67, from Cambridgeshire, was diagnosed with Alzheimer's in January and is the first person to begin treatment on the trial, called AD-SMART.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "We have Alzheimer's in the family," she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "My mother had it and my aunts, so it was a disappointment rather than a shock when I was diagnosed because I knew it would restrict my life.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "But I was determined that it wasn't going to define me." Angela said she felt empowered joining the trial because "at least you are doing something".
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "Instead of just sitting there, you're standing up and saying, I will fight back." Alzheimer's is the most common type of dementia, affecting around 600,000 people in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham, whose father died from Alzheimer's last month, said he knew how it felt to lose a loved one to dementia, and had seen first-hand the devastating impact of the disease on families.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: "That's why I'm proud to see this trial being launched in the UK, so that cutting-edge treatments can reach patients here as soon as possible," he said.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: The AD-SMART study is what's known as a multi-arm, multi-stage platform trial where several treatments are tested simultaneously, with the results compared with one group of participants taking a placebo or dummy.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: This means those involved have a higher likelihood of getting an active treatment than in a traditional trial.
sentences.article_title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study

sentences.text: If any drug isn't showing benefit it can be dropped quickly and a new treatment added in its place - the approach has been used successfully in cancer and motor neurone disease.

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has asked ministers to develop a plan to remove standing charges from gas bills.

sentences.text: These are fixed daily fees that cover the costs of connecting to a supply.

sentences.text: During Prime Minister's Questions, Burnham said the "pragmatic decision" on giving the green light to the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea would allow the government to increase investment in renewables and "do more to help people with bills".

sentences.text: He said he had asked the Chancellor John Healey and Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh "to look at whether we can remove standing charges from gas bills and to report back to this house at the earliest opportunity".

sentences.text: No details have been given on how removing standing charges would work in practice.

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell says the government will "update and strengthen" Holocaust education within schools after a major review highlighted the "shocking scale" of antisemitism in British society.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Schools and colleges in England will be required to recognise antisemitism as a distinct category of harm and take explicit action against it.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It means anti-Jewish hatred will be treated as a specific safeguarding risk rather than being dealt with through existing measures to stop racism and bullying.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The government has accepted all of the 27 recommendations made in the government-commissioned review including dedicated training for teachers and more consistent recording of incidents.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says The review into antisemitism in schools and colleges in England was led by former Ofsted chief inspector Sir David Bell and presented to Parliament on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Powell told the BBC it marked a "generational moment" to re-educate young people, among whom she said the issue of antisemitism was "particularly prevalent".
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: She said: "It's definitely a crisis and I think it's actually got worse since Sir David began this review.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: This has become a real challenge for Jewish people in our country, but also Jewish students and Jewish teachers working in our schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "I do really feel it is a generational moment to educate this generation and the next – that is the job of education – to understand what antisemitism is in the modern world." Speaking on Holocaust education, the education secretary said new lessons will "challenge" some of the concepts that young people have.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review also calls for stronger guidance on political impartiality for teachers.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Powell told the House of Commons "teachers should not bring their own political views into the classroom" but they should not avoid discussing important topics.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review was launched following a series of high-profile incidents including the attack at Heaton Park synagogue in Manchester in October 2025, in which two men were killed.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Separate reviews were also commissioned into antisemitism in healthcare and into public order and hate crime laws.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The BBC revealed in August that the Bell review had found Jewish schoolchildren were experiencing regular harassment and abuse.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It also found that headteachers of some Jewish schools were spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than educational matters .
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review also recommends that the government sets up a type of hotline where school leaders can access immediate advice on tackling antisemitism.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Bell, who is now vice-chancellor of the University of Sunderland, heard evidence from pupils, teachers, governors and parents across state and independent schools, as well as from community organisations.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: He told the BBC: "This is not just a report for Jewish children in Jewish schools.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: This is for all children and young people in all schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: We know that antisemitism crosses all boundaries." Earlier this month, the BBC was given rare access inside a Jewish school in Hertfordshire, where pupils and staff operate under tight security, amid heightened concerns about antisemitism.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Spencer Lewis, the executive headteacher of Yavneh College, said that security was an "innate part" of his role.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "When you come in in the morning, there are high gates, high fences, lots of security cameras.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: We have four full-time security staff.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: And it sort of just becomes part of what you do," he said.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "We think about it a lot." In response to the recommendations, the government will also encourage schools to adopt the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA)'s working definition of antisemitism, although it cannot make it compulsory.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The definition is supported by mainstream Jewish organisations and has been adopted by 47 countries, including the UK, as well as most British universities.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: However, some of the IHRA definition's examples of antisemitic behaviour have proven controversial.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The Board of Deputies of British Jews said that adopting the IHRA definition would provide schools with a tool "to deepen understanding of contemporary antisemitism".
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "Antisemitism in our schools is real, it is widespread, and too often it goes unrecognised and unchallenged." "One-off assemblies are not enough, and neither is sitting pupils in front of a video.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Young people need the space to ask difficult questions, challenge their own assumptions and understand that antisemitism did not start or end with the Holocaust." The National Education Union raised concerns about creating a "hierarchy of racism" and adopting the IHRA definition.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It said the latter risked "blurring the line between antisemitism and legitimate criticism of the Israeli government and the genocide in Gaza".
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The union welcomed a "strengthened focus on antisemitism" while underlining that "no form of racism should be minimised".
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Recent figures from the Community Security Trust, an organisation which provides security advice and support to the Jewish community, showed a spike in antisemitic incidents at schools.

sentences.text: Watch the full film of Ed Thomas's investigation here , external Our reporter contacted Alias on the phone, claiming to be a business owner who faced a fine after immigration officers had found somebody working at his mini-mart illegally.

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham opened Number 10 North in July A "mindset shift" is needed across the UK's central government to help Number 10 North deliver its objectives, its deputy director has said.
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: Duncan Parish told a conference in Lincolnshire on Wednesday there were "institutional challenges" within government that needed to be overcome to deliver change.
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: The Manchester office of Number 10 North - sister to London's Downing Street - was set up by Prime Minister Andy Burnham in July.
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: Burnham's political opponents have called the office a "gimmick" and raised transparency concerns about the costs involved.
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: Speaking to the Great Exhibition conference of local political and business leaders, Parish said his career in the civil service to date had "not been without its frustrations" and there can be "friction" between different parts of government which have "similar but ever so slightly competing objectives".
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: Parish, a civil servant in Whitehall before moving to Manchester four years ago, said Number 10 North staff were "delivering outcomes at a national level across a huge range of areas" including health, transport, education and social care.
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: "But we continually need to work to overcome those institutional challenges," he added.
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: He said one priority of Number 10 North was to "shift power and accountability" closer to local areas, but acknowledged "that means reforming the civil service as well" - by not viewing national, regional and local government as separate.
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: "But to deliver that change, requires us all to change - and part of that change is a mindset shift within central government," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: In September, Conservative shadow minister Mike Wood raised concerns about "little information and so little transparency" surrounding Number 10 North which he described as a "gimmick".
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: "The minister either doesn't know or won't tell us how much No 10 North will cost, how many people work there or how many of them actually turn up to work - it's almost as though this hasn't been properly thought through," he told a House of Commons debate.
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: He called for the annual budget, staff levels and office attendance statistics to be published.
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: Current staffing levels have also not yet been clarified.
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: Cabinet Office minister Sally Jameson said last week that the government did not know how much has been spent on hotels for No 10 North staff, ministers and special advisers travelling between London and Manchester since it opened.
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: The cost is "not centrally collated" but is "being met within existing departmental budgets", Jameson said in response to a parliamentary question.
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: Number 10 North's latest summit of regional mayors, held in its "situation room", will take place on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: Burnham has previously indicated he will work there at least once a week, and hosted the Irish Taoiseach Micheál Martin in September .
sentences.article_title: 'Mindset shift' needed within government on No10 North, says deputy

sentences.text: Parish added in his speech: "How will we know if Number 10 North is working?

sentences.text: He told the jury he had been diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder in 2015 and that it had been triggered in 2021.
sentences.article_title: Civil servant admits he 'made mistakes' juggling five government jobs

sentences.text: He told the court that staff and managers at the Department for Environment and Rural Affairs (Defra), the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, East London NHS Trust and the Department for Health and Social Care (DHSC) all knew he had jobs elsewhere.
sentences.article_title: Civil servant admits he 'made mistakes' juggling five government jobs

sentences.text: At the height of the alleged deceit, Chowdhury held five full-time jobs on full-time salaries within the public sector.

sentences.text: In the spring of 2023, he was employed by the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the UK Health Security Agency, the Food Standards Agency, the Department for Business and Trade and the Home Office.

sentences.text: The jury was told that throughout this period he was contracted to work 183 hours a week - more than the number of hours that exist in seven days.

sentences.text: Each job paid a full-time wage, with Chowdhury paid £11,000 for a single month's work in 2023.
sentences.article_title: Civil servant admits he 'made mistakes' juggling five government jobs

sentences.text: The Unite union has hit out at a plan by NatWest to reduce the rights of 30,000 of its employees to work from home.

sentences.article_title: Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office

sentences.article_title: Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office

sentences.article_title: Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office

sentences.article_title: Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office

sentences.article_title: Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office

sentences.text: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman has won a dismissal of a lawsuit brought against him by his sister that claimed he had sexually abused her more than two decades ago.

sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey says he wants to avoid an investor exodus from the UK Chancellor John Healey has dismissed calls from some Labour MPs to increase Capital Gains Tax (CGT).
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: Cabinet ministers Wes Streeting and Louise Haigh both previously voiced support for raising CGT before Andy Burnham became prime minister in July.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: Ahead of next week's Budget, as first reported by the Times , external , Healey is minded not to increase CGT - which is imposed on the profit people make when they sell an asset that has increased in value, such as shares in a company or properties which are not primary residences.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: The move followed warnings that it could end up costing the government money if wealthy people leave the country or defer selling off assets.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: If you pay income tax at the basic rate then CGT is charged at 18%.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: For higher and additional rate income tax payers, the CGT rate is 24%.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: Last year, HMRC estimated , external that lifting the lower rate of CGT by 1% could raise £5m by 2028-9 but increasing the higher rate of CGT by 10% would reduce the Treasury's receipts by £3.6bn in 2028-9.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: The amount raised could be reduced if people adapt their behaviour to the tax rise, for example by moving abroad or deciding not to sell a property.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: The chancellor gave an indication of his approach last month in a speech when he spoke about the importance of businesses and self-employed people making profits.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: "I want to see this country as a country of wealth creation.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: I want our government decisions and policies to raise the levels of confidence, and investment, and profit in British business," Healey said.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: Burnham has faced warnings against lifting CGT.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: His former adviser and Goldman Sachs Chief Economist Lord Jim O'Neill suggested it would send "the wrong message to business".
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: But influential Labour figures had pushed for equalising CGT and income tax, with the former generally attracting a lower tax rate.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: Louise Haigh, a key ally of the prime minister, had suggested capital gains should go up to be closer to income tax, before she became Burnham's first secretary of state.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: In an article for the Renewal journal, , external Haigh argued that raising CGT would "shift the taxation burden away from punishing work, and towards unproductive capital accumulation which does little to grow the everyday economy".
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: She said this could be accompanied by measures to ensure that "genuine investment returns are not penalised".
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: He had argued that equalising CGT with income tax would address an unfair system that was "penalising work".
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: Asked about the government's plans for CGT on BBC Breakfast, Communities Secretary Angela Rayner would not speculate on the Budget.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: Pressed over whether rejecting calls to increase the tax was a win for the rich, she said the government had already taken steps to give people "breathing space" and help with the cost of living.
sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.article_title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget

sentences.text: President Donald Trump has been boasting about the performance of the US economy ahead of the midterm congressional elections, claiming he has boosted incomes, reduced inflation and created jobs.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The US economy is also being helped by an AI investment boom, and could falter if that spending were to dry up.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: So how does all this feel for the average American?
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: BBC Verify has looked at whether the evidence supports the president's claims.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The overall US economy is growing at a respectable clip by the country's recent historic standards.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The latest data shows US GDP , external - which is how economists measure the size of the US economy - currently expanding at an annualised rate of 2.2%.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: And it has increased by around 3.2% overall since the end of 2024, just before Trump took office for his second term.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That is more growth than any other member of the G7 group of leading economies over that period.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The US growth rate has been faster than was forecast by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) , external in the immediate wake of Trump's announcement of a swathe of new tariffs on goods coming into the US on 2 April 2025.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: It downgraded its forecasts at the time, citing the negative impact of Trump's import duties on investment and consumer spending.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Though it is important to note that Trump eased the tariffs considerably in the months that followed, reducing the impact that had initially been expected on the economy.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The US economy has also been heavily supported in recent years by American technology companies making massive investments in AI, including by constructing data centres around the country.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Spending on building data centres , external (excluding the IT hardware to go in them) by US businesses in August 2026 was $5bn, almost double the monthly rate when Trump returned to office.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Many American voters wanted to punish Joe Biden in the 2024 presidential election, holding him responsible for the pain caused by a significant spike in prices in the wake of the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The current rate of US inflation , external is 3.7%.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That's still well down on the recent peak rate of 9% under Biden in 2022, but higher than the 3% rate that Donald Trump inherited in January 2025.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Economists estimate , external US inflation would have been lower without the new tariffs imposed by Trump since he returned to office.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: While the impact of the Iran war on global energy prices, with the significant disruption to oil and fuel supplies from the Middle East, has also helped push up US domestic inflation.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The price of a gallon of diesel in the US , external - a fuel used not only by drivers but also widely in agriculture and industry - hit a record high of $6.52 in September.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The price of some grocery staples , external like beef and coffee have risen since Trump returned to office, though the price of eggs has fallen.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: And some US retailers have warned , external that rising energy prices caused by the Iran war will make producing food more expensive and raise prices at the till.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Average US household incomes are still rising under Trump.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The median income - after adjusting for inflation - rose 2.6% in 2025 to $87,460, the highest on record , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The richest 1%, by contrast, are estimated to be an average of $12,560 better off than they woud have been, primarily because of Trump's tax cuts.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: ITEP's estimates about the impact of tariffs on American households of different income levels are broadly similar to those of the Tax Foundation think tank , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Trump predicted his tariffs would result in America being "flooded with jobs" , external as manufacturing firms set up new factories on US soil to avoid their products being taxed at the border.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Since he returned to the White House, an average of 34,000 jobs have been added to the economy each month. ​​But that is significantly down on the 122,000 jobs added each month in the final year of Biden's presidency , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: And the number of Americans employed in manufacturing , external - 12.6 million in September 2026 - is slightly lower than it was when Trump's second term began.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: However, the US unemployment rate remains relatively low , external at 4.2%, which is broadly where it was when Trump returned to the White House.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Part of the reason for this is Trump's immigration crackdown and deportation programme, which has reduced the size of the available US workforce , external and means a lower number of jobs need to be created each month to stop unemployment rising.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: US government borrowing has increased in Trump's second term, partly driven up by his significant tax cuts .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The federal government deficit - the gap between its revenues from taxes and its spending - was $2 trillion in the year to September 2026 , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That's equivalent to around 6% , external of US GDP.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: And the US deficit is projected to rise to above 8% of GDP by 2030 , external .
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That high rate of government borrowing is itself helping to boost US GDP growth.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The IMF has warned that excessive US government borrowing , external , which it uses to bridge the deficit, and its rapidly rising national debt are raising the risk of a future financial crisis in America.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: This would have a deeply damaging impact on most American households.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The growing deficit is also one of the reasons the US government gets charged more to borrow money in financial markets.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The 10-year US government bond yield has risen sharply since Trump returned to office in January 2025 and is now above 5%, the highest rate since the global financial crisis in 2007.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That increase in the market cost of US government borrowing also puts upward pressure on the interest rates on mortgages available to American households.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: The interest rate on a new 30-year US mortgage has risen to 7.4% , external per year, up from 6.9% when Trump returned to the White House.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: That's added to problems in the US housing market, making homes less affordable for new buyers.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: It has left many existing owners reluctant to move because doing so would mean giving up their cheaper mortgages, which they took out at lower rates , external and cannot take with them to a new property.
sentences.article_title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?

sentences.text: Drivers will be given the right to challenge "rip-off" private parking charges and more grace when using private providers under new rules set out by Andy Burnham.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: The prime minister announced the changes after concerns were raised that penalties issued by private providers were too harsh and left motorists unfairly punished.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: The new rules include a cancellation of charges for honest mistakes such as stopping to check directions and for non-payment due to broken ticket machines.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: Drivers will also get a 10-minute window to leave a car park without facing a penalty.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: Motoring groups welcomed the changes, but said more needed to be done to stop charges when the driver had done nothing wrong.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: Private car parks are different to council-owned car parks and streets, but more tickets at private sites are now being issued than ever recorded.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: According to RAC analysis of government data, some 17 million private parking tickets were issued in 2025-26, a 17% increase from a year earlier.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: With each charge worth up to £100, the data suggests drivers could collectively face private parking charges worth more than £4.6m each day.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: In one case, a woman was taken to court in a £1,906 claim after taking longer than five minutes to pay at a car park in Derby .
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: The charge was eventually dropped .
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: "Being a few minutes late back to your car or typing one digit of your number plate wrong shouldn't end with a hefty fine landing on your doormat," said Burnham.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: He added that such charges left "people feeling ripped off and out of pocket".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: In 2019, an act of Parliament was passed to create a code but the code was withdrawn in 2022, due to "resistance from the private parking industry", according to the RAC.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: The current industry Code of Practice, created by the British Parking Association and the International Parking Community, was introduced in 2024 and updated last year after a review .
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: Angela Rayner, the Communities and Housing Secretary, told BBC Breakfast that parking "shouldn't be a way of making money".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: Asked if the changes were an admission that motorists have been "ripped off" by parking companies for years, she said: "We're calling time on it.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: They have regulated themselves and they have their appeals process but we're giving it more meat now." She said the current level of fine was a "proportionate response to when people don't follow the rules".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered to take action over odours Milpitas, an affluent city in California's Silicon Valley tech hub, has an odour problem.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: For decades, residents have had to endure rank smells wafting from industrial sites, among them a 342-acre landfill.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "When I first moved here, I could not open my window for over 10 years," says Chia-Ling Kong, an engineer for a tech firm who lives around half a mile from the dump.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: While things have got better in recent years, Kong says she and her neighbours must still contend with around "two or three hours of bad smells a day".
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Perhaps befitting Silicon Valley, the community is putting its hopes in technology.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered by local authorities to use drones and install monitors to systematically track and measure the chemicals responsible for bad odours.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: They have also been told to automate the collection of landfill gases responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Kong is optimistic a data-driven approach will make a difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Hopefully with this continuous monitoring, it makes it easier to pinpoint problems at the moment it starts." The operators of the landfill say they are committed to operating it safely and protecting air quality.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Just like in Milpitas, where Kong is part of a citizen's campaign against the odours, communities around the world are raising a stink about bad smells making day-to-day life miserable.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Sometimes a rubbish dump is to blame, or it might be a sewage treatment works, or a reeking factory.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: When the complaints start stacking up, resolving them is not always simple.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Many countries have no regulations in place dictating how to manage smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In the US, for example, the Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This leaves states and local governments to take charge of the issue.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Urban sprawl is often part of the problem, bringing communities closer to stinky facilities that may historically have been kept at a distance.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This is creating more demand for technologies to monitor and prevent smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour consultant Micheal Bull says people are increasingly concerned about neighbourhood stinks.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "You're getting developments being built nearer to odorous processes… as land has become more valuable, there is also infilling," Bull says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: He is speaking about his experiences in the UK, but it's a similar story in many parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites are among the most difficult to resolve The technologies used to tackle industrial pongs generally fall into three categories: they absorb odours; convert them into something less smelly through a chemical reaction; or burn them away.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Experts on fixing industrial odours say that the best technologies, when used correctly, can remove 90% or more of the target compounds responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But this can be expensive and some operators opt for simpler and cheaper solutions.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: These include masking odours from landfill or sewage processing by spraying giant quantities of deodorisers.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour experts contacted for this article were dubious about the effectiveness of such industrial scale air fresheners.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "In my view they're not likely to change the odours," says Bull, who likens them to fabric conditioner.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites – a common cause of complaints – are among the stinkiest and most difficult to resolve, according to Carlos Diaz, an environmental consultant based in Spain.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Landfill is difficult to treat because you have a very large surface," he says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In some places at least, technology is making a real difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Residents in Des Moines, Iowa, have long complained of the so-called Eastside Funk, a putrid scent that residents report drifts over parts of the city.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: A study commissioned by city authorities showed that a trio of industrial meat companies were among culprits.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Within 10 miles, there's about half a million people," says Dalton Jacobus, who works in the Department of Neighborhood Services.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "If the winds are out of the wrong direction, 100,000 people can be in the middle of that odour plume." The authorities are now paying around $240,000 (£182,000) a year on technology to track the stink, so they can take action.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "What we wanted to do was build a ring of odour monitors around the facilities that we suspected of emitting odours," says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The monitors, which measure levels of chemical compounds in the air, work in combination with a weather station to provide real-time data on the concentrations that are coming from each facility based off the wind patterns.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This has put an end to finger pointing about who's to blame each time a smell sparks complaints, says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Smithfield Foods, which operates a meat processing in Des Moines, says it has invested $2m to install a regenerative thermal oxidiser that destroys the chemicals associated with bad smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Even so, the company says it does not believe it is the source of odour complaints.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Before installing the monitors – which some local companies help pay for – officials in Des Moines would drive out to the source of a complaint to sniff the air.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Relying on the human nose to sniff out industrial smells is still commonplace.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Claudia Barrios Obregón from Kunak, the company behind the monitors in Des Moines, says: "Right now, the way that cities control or measure odours is olfactometry: a human panel measures and gives an opinion of what the odour is like.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But that's not that realistic." The Spanish company's monitors are an example of so-called electronic noses that make it easier to detect smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Whatever technology is used, it can be hard to keep everyone happy, as smells are so subjective.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, the general rule is that the nastier we perceive the odour to be, the more sensitive towards it we are," says Johan Lundström, a professor in the science of smell at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm, Sweden.

sentences.text: Bereaved families affected by severe delays paying out civil service pensions could face an "unjust" tax bill, the government has been warned.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Under HMRC rules, certain lump sum pension payments must be paid within two years of the pension scheme being notified of a death to remain tax-free.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Conservative MP Sir Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, who chairs Parliament's Public Accounts Committee, said it was "unconscionable" some families could face a "death tax" through no fault of their own.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: The Cabinet Office said that if delays caused a tax charge there were existing avenues to claim compensation, such as the Pensions Ombudsman.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: However, the ombudsman is currently advising that standard complaints are only likely to be resolved within 18 months, with more complex cases facing a longer wait.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: The Civil Service Pension scheme manages the pensions of 1.7 million public sector workers in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Outsourcing firm Capita took over the administration of the scheme from a company called MyCSP in December 2025, saying it inherited a backlog of more than 86,000 cases.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Despite a two-year transition period to prepare for the takeover, problems have persisted and by February the backlog had grown to 120,000 cases.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Retired civil servants and bereaved families have been left waiting months for pension payments, with some struggling to pay bills.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Civil service pension backlog 'overwhelmed' Capita, boss says Emergency loans offered to civil servants waiting on pensions Retired civil servants left in pension limbo According to the latest figures up to 30 September , external , 1,643 outstanding cases of bereavement or death in service are more than 100 days old.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Of these, only 301 are in scope to be paid within 15 days.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: The PCS union, which represents civil servants, said that while not all these cases would ultimately be affected by the two-year tax rule, there were "serious questions" over how long they would remain unresolved.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: The Cabinet Office said that while the number of individuals approaching the two-year threshold was currently fewer than 10, "we are treating every case with urgency".
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: If someone dies before the age of 75, a pension lump sum death benefit is only tax-free if it is paid within two years of the pension scheme first becoming aware of the death, and if the value is below the deceased's Lump Sum and Death Benefit Allowance.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: The payment would be taxed at the same rate as the beneficiary's income tax rate.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Sir Geoffrey has written to Cabinet Office Minister Louise Haigh to urge the government to confirm the bereaved families affected will not face this "unjust financial penalty".
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: His letter came after BBC Radio 4's Money Box Live highlighted the potential tax liability.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Sir Geoffrey said "the chaos currently engulfing the Civil Service Pension Scheme means that the likelihood of death benefit payments being made within two years is slim".
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: He warned "a significant number" of family members "will be watching the clock quickly tick down to a year, as the maladministration of the scheme enters its tenth month".
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: He added: "This is an additional stress they should not have to bear." Writing in response to Sir Geoffrey's letter, Minister Sally Jameson said neither the Cabinet Office nor the pension scheme administrator had the power under tax law to alter or waive these tax charges.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: However, she said where delays lead to an avoidable tax charge people "will not be left out of pocket" and the pension scheme "will ensure compensation is processed swiftly".
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: She added that the Cabinet Office was working with Capita to ensure the oldest outstanding cases were prioritised.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: "It's a bitter pill to swallow to have to pay tax for something which was not my fault," he said.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: "It creates unnecessary worry and anguish through the process, which is already in itself difficult." Rob said he needed the money to cover the estate costs he had to pay for his brother and fill a £20,000 hole in his savings.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: However, he said it was "heartbreaking" to hear of other cases where people needed the money just to survive.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Rob added that the idea that he might face "another battle" to recoup the tax through compensation made it feel like "you just want to give up".
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Rob has been waiting almost two years for the lump sum from his brother's civil service pension Fran Heathcote, head of the PCS union, said it would be "a profound injustice" if families faced a further financial penalty because of Capita's failures.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: "If that does happen, the government should be ashamed that families are being made to pay the price for failures that are entirely outside their control," she said.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the Cabinet Office, which has overall responsibility for the Civil Service Pension Scheme, said: "The service levels following the move to Capita have been completely unacceptable and we are committed to ensuring no member is left financially worse off.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: "We are continuing to hold Capita to account, including holding back nearly £10m in payments, and are doing everything in our power to ensure that individuals do not experience delays.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: "If delays cause a tax charge, existing avenues for complaints can provide financial redress or compensation to cover losses." sentences.text: Rhun ap Iorwerth delivered a speech about devolution to Cardiff University on Monday evening The Welsh government is to examine the powers councils have and how authorities work together regionally, the first minister has announced.
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: At a speech at Cardiff University, Rhun ap Iorwerth announced that this could lead to new legislation after the next election in 2030.
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: "Whilst I am clear that we should never assume that what works for England will work for Wales, and vice versa - and I hope the prime minister acknowledges this - I know that our current arrangements aren't perfect either.
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: "I am convinced that, over time, Wales should move towards a more coherent and more streamlined system of local and regional governance.
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: The first minister said it would be a "detailed, meaningful exercise reflecting on where powers and specific competences should lie, how regional working works best and what effective cooperation looks like".
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: Rhun ap Iorwerth is set to meet Andy Burnham at the end of the month Asked by BBC Wales if he was trying to offer the prime minister a "quid pro quo", ap Iorwerth said: "I don't quite see it in that way.
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: "As somebody who wants power close to the people in Wales, I like the fact that the UK's new prime minister is talking that kind of language, but it means different things in Wales and England.
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: "The devolution programme that we're hearing from Andy Burnham is largely an England programme.
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: What I want to do is find common ground with him." The first minister questioned whether Downing Street's "devolution agenda" was "really an England-only agenda", and whether it came to a "shuddering halt at Offa's Dyke".
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: Economic development in Wales is devolved to the Welsh government.
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: But ap Iorwerth said Wales was living with a "confused" and "increasingly fragmented system".
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: "A succession of UK government programmes has been layered on top of devolved responsibilities and in some cases undermining them," he said.
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: "Some have funded worthwhile projects.
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: Some have brought genuine benefits.
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: But, taken together, they have made the landscape more complicated, more fragmented and more difficult to navigate." He listed city and growth deals, and the former Conservative UK government's levelling up and shared prosperity fund projects, as examples.
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: "If powers have been devolved, central government should not continue to duplicate them," he said.
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: He called for a "practical agreement about how our two governments work together to unlock Wales' economic potential".
sentences.article_title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers

sentences.text: "Whatever we have, lets look at what works well and how we can improve it," the first minister said.

sentences.text: The decision to grant approval for drilling at the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea and the further delay in a decision about the Rosebank oil field, also in the North Sea, are case studies in the slow-motion awkwardness the UK has collectively had, over years, about energy.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: At the heart of that awkwardness, these questions: where should our energy come from, and with what costs and consequences, for the customer and for the environment?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Since becoming prime minister, Andy Burnham has talked about a desire to be "pragmatic" about the North Sea as he puts it, which is why this decision about Jackdaw isn't a surprise.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: In fact it felt near inevitable after President Trump blurted out – after his first phone call with Burnham in the summer – that the prime minister had told him he would "open up the North Sea".
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Burnham acknowledged the two leaders had discussed the issue, arguing: "There is a resource there.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: When people are struggling - you can't ignore that." What we now know is the government is approving drilling of the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea, about 150 miles east of Aberdeen.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: A decision on Rosebank, an oil field about 80 miles north east of Shetland, is expected to take a bit longer.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: UK government approves Jackdaw gas field and says production will start this month The city caught in the middle of the big energy shift debate What is happening with the Jackdaw and Rosebank gas and oil fields?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: The timeline of back and forth about both projects is worth revisiting.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Jackdaw was first approved four years ago, Rosebank three years ago.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: But after a legal challenge by environmental campaigners, it was ruled that consent had been granted unlawfully and there needed to be a more detailed assessment of the environmental impact.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: And then, of course – there is politics, international and domestic, between parties and within parties.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Debate about energy security and spiralling prices, given the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, the environmental impact, carbon emissions and the message new drilling sends to the wider world.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: But others point to the extra carbon emissions when energy is imported, the tax revenues generated from domestic energy and the social and economic consequences of the British oil and gas sector deindustrialising too quickly and, in particular, the impact on cities such as Aberdeen.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Then, for the government, there are the promises the Labour Party made when it was seeking your support at the general election in 2024.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Page 52 of Labour's manifesto reads like a rhetorical twister – a paragraph of promises seeking to stretch in multiple directions at the same time, trying to keep a breadth of people happy simultaneously, or perhaps not annoy too many people too much.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: "Labour will not revoke existing licences and we will partner with business and workers to manage our existing fields for the entirety of their lifespan.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Crucially, oil and gas production in the North Sea will be with us for decades to come, and the North Sea will be managed in a way that does not jeopardise jobs," it reads.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: "And our offshore workers will lead the world in the industries of the future.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: We will not issue new licences to explore new fields because they will not take a penny off bills, cannot make us energy secure, and will only accelerate the worsening climate crisis," it adds.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Crucially, the Jackdaw and Rosebank licences had already been issued, leaving political wriggle room on these two outstanding and high profile decisions the Labour government inherited on taking office.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: But the multiple trade-offs, of course, remain very real, including for some of the key individuals involved.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Miatta Fahnbulleh took over from Ed Miliband as energy secretary earlier this yer Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who used to be the energy secretary, has long been vocal about what he sees as the need to move away from fossil fuels.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Instead, she is grounding her argument for approving this in energy security and saying the tax revenue generated will go into an "Energy Wealth Fund" to pay for "low carbon and renewable projects".
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Rosebank, she added, was a "different proposition" as its oil would be exported, but she will "look at it".
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Politically, the decision on Jackdaw is considerably easier for the government than the decision on Rosebank.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Broadly speaking, most Labour MPs are comfortable with endorsing Jackdaw.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: It is also a project backed by the Conservatives and Reform (who argue a decision should have been taken much sooner) and the Scottish National Party and the Liberal Democrats.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: The Green Party of England and Wales are opposed.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: On Rosebank, the argument is much more contentious within the Labour Party.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Some, who can see the rationale for Jackdaw cannot see it for Rosebank.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: Bluntly, it is a much more difficult decision, as Fahnbulleh has acknowledged.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: What we can expect in the coming hours and days - as it has started already - is a resumption of all the arguments these projects have already provoked, with some saying approval should have happened ages ago, alongside plenty more.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

sentences.text: And others arguing the announcement is utterly irresponsible.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain
