sentences.text: The sixth report of the Covid inquiry is highly critical of the way the government tried to protect people in care settings in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Around 500,000 people were living in care homes at the start of the pandemic – with another million receiving care in their own homes.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The inquiry said action to protect them came too late, causing devastating consequences.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: There were more than 43,000 recorded deaths involving Covid in care homes between March 2020 and July 2022.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Here are the key findings of the 287-page report.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: At the start of the pandemic, the then-health secretary in England, Matt Hancock, said the UK government had placed "a protective ring" around care homes.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But the inquiry says this was not the case, listing a catalogue of failings.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: It says the care sector appeared to be "something of an afterthought".
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: A lack of personal protective equipment (PPE) meant staff had to resort to makeshift workarounds, including bin bags, festival waterproof ponchos and painters' overalls.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The report is also critical of the way hospital patients who may be infected with Covid were moved to care homes to make space for others.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The decision was understandable given the need to free up beds for Covid patients.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But, without sufficient testing, it was important to keep these people separate and isolate them from others in case they were infected.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Official guidance in March 2020 in England, Wales and Northern Ireland did not request this.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: That, the report says, was a significant oversight.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: When the pandemic started, high levels of staff vacancies and turnover in the social care sector meant that the workforce was "fragile and lacking resilience".
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: This undermined the ability of the sector to respond to the pandemic, the inquiry says.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: For example, care homes tend to rely heavily on agency staff who work in a variety of different homes.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But a desire not to have staff going into multiple homes, to reduce the risk of infection transmission, meant staff shortages got even worse.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Financially, care providers struggled too, as the number of people using services dropped.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: And for a sector that uses zero-hours contracts, there was a lack of financial support to help care staff stay off work if there was concern they might be infected.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The response also suffered because of the fragmented nature of the system, with thousands of different providers and services overseen by councils.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: It meant the sector was more distant from government than the NHS.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The pandemic, the inquiry said, exposed and exacerbated these existing weaknesses.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The report is clear that precautionary steps taken to restrict visiting, as part of infection control, went too far.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: It acknowledges there was little choice to introduce bans on visitors at the start of the pandemic, saying that was rational.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But as the pandemic progressed, so did the balance between the benefits and harms of restrictions.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Visits are extremely important, allowing loved ones to help residents with everything from personal care to maintaining their mental health.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: By September 2020, evidence suggested visitors posed a "marginal risk" – staff were judged to be the key entry point for infections.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The four UK nations then started to relax their guidance, but many care homes failed to implement this and visiting remained heavily restricted.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: This, says the inquiry, resulted in a significant decline in the health and wellbeing of residents.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation), including chest compressions, can be life-saving if a person's heart has stopped beating.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But doctors can sometimes opt not to resuscitate people - as can individuals themselves in advance - for example, if the individual is extremely frail or has a life-limiting illness.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: This should be done on an individual basis and the use of blanket do not resuscitate orders (DNACPR) is considered unlawful.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The inquiry says it heard evidence of GPs imposing blanket DNACPRs on care home residents.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: And it pointed to records showing a sharp increase in orders being put in place – they jumped from 16,800 to 26,500 in the first nine months of the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: This concern mirrors an earlier Care Quality Commission investigation which found evidence of unacceptable and inappropriate DNACPRs being put in place.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The impact on staff working in care homes was huge, affecting their mental health and wellbeing, the inquiry said.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Some moved into the care homes where they worked, in an attempt to protect residents from infection.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: One care home owner in Wales described how 39 staff moved in for a fortnight at the start of the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Seeing so many residents die placed an enormous strain on workers, who often had to provide end-of-life care to multiple people at the same time.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: One care home, for example, lost half of its residents over the course of three weeks.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Staff told the inquiry of the deep distress they suffered.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: "Staff were sitting on video calls with families, saying their last goodbye to loved ones.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: That was horrendous… staff were crying with the residents, because it was just so emotional for them," one said.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Government failures in care settings created an environment that allowed Covid to spread like wildfire, an official inquiry has said.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: The sixth report from the Covid inquiry said the care sector appeared to be "something of an afterthought" in the early stages of the pandemic and there was no "protective ring" put around homes as claimed by ministers at the time.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: There were more than 43,000 recorded deaths involving Covid in care homes between March 2020 and July 2022.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: The 287-page report also highlighted shortages of PPE for carers and criticised the way hospital patients were discharged into care homes.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: It said limits on visits caused enormous harm to residents and their loved ones, though it blamed this on care homes themselves.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: Around 1.5 million adults were either living in care homes or receiving support in their own homes when Covid hit.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: Action to protect them came too late, causing devastating consequences, the inquiry said.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: Chair Baroness Hallet said a lack of testing, PPE and pre-pandemic planning combined with policy decisions early on "created an environment in which the virus could spread like wildfire".
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: "At the critical early stages of the pandemic, not enough was done to protect those living and working in care homes," she said.
sentences.article_title: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds

sentences.text: An AI tool may be able to help doctors judge how ill a patient is using a single photograph of their face, say US researchers.

sentences.text: Trained on millions of healthy faces, and 35,000 photos of cancer patients, the tool can make estimates on survival by looking closely at features near the eyes, the scientists say.

sentences.text: While it's a long way from being suitable for use in hospitals, the researchers say their goal is to help doctors recommend the right treatments for their patients.

sentences.text: The preliminary findings are published in the Lancet Digital Health , external journal.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The researchers developed two AI tools to estimate biological age and predict cancer survival from a single face photo.

sentences.text: Areas shown in yellow had the greatest impact on predictions.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The 'FaceSurvival' AI tool suggests the area under the eyes and around the bridge of the nose are the most vital parts of the face to assess when estimating how long they might have left to live.

sentences.text: These metrics applied across many different types of cancers, varying in severity, including ones that had spread to the patient's bones or brain.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .

sentences.text: A second head teachers' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections in England, saying it is "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale" of its members.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: The Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) also raised the prospect of potential strike action, saying a new grading system had become an "overbearing mess".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: The Department for Education (DfE) said ministers were "working with Ofsted and school leaders to ensure accountability is fair, proportionate and focused on helping every school get better".

sentences.text: ASCL's announcement comes after another union, the National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) , said changes Ofsted made to inspections just under a year ago had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.

sentences.text: ASCL said it had passed a motion of no confidence in "the ability of Ofsted's leadership to address the damage being done by the new inspection system", adding that it was "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale of members".

sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: "The current system is not fit for purpose.

sentences.text: The amount of time children in England spend on screens at school could be harming their "physical and developmental health", a group of more than 150 clinicians has warned.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: GPs, paediatricians and other specialists said in an open letter to Education Secretary Lucy Powell and Health Secretary Yvette Cooper that tablets and laptops are being used without a full understanding of their long-term health impacts, including on eye health.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The clinicians said they are prescribing glasses, hearing aids and speech therapy to children "for a problem that is unintentionally being made worse in our schools".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The government said it was consulting on screen time guidance for children aged five to 18 but that technology could be a powerful learning tool if used properly.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The group of clinicians said nearly one million children are using screens in most lessons, despite studies suggesting a rise in short-sightedness.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: They pointed to an analysis of 276 studies covering 5.4 million participants around the world.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: That analysis, they claimed, found a rise in short-sightedness among children and adolescents from around 24% in 1990 to almost 36% by 2023, warning the condition is associated with an increased risk of a range of eye health problems.

sentences.text: She told BBC Radio 4's Today programme parents had not been given the chance to "opt out" of the "excessive" use of screens in schools, which risks children "just not thriving" in education.

sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: It is one of the reasons she supports the decision to rename PCOS to polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) earlier this year, alongside a recommendation for annual health checks to improve diagnosis and long-term care.

Rochelle Lewis said years of symptoms and appointments left her feeling unheard For many years, Rochelle Lewis, from Wolverhampton, struggled with facial hair growth, painful periods and anxiety.
sentences.article_title: Women welcome annual health checks for condition affecting millions

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: All three companies have appeared in court this week, arguing they should not need to provide so much information in response to Ofcom's formal requests.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta has separately also argued Ofcom should not be able to levy fines for breaches based on its global annual revenue.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: It also contends that its messaging and image-sharing apps should not have to face additional requirements under the OSA, such as tackling paid-for fraud ads.

sentences.text: A woman convinced her former partner she had given birth to two children who most likely did not exist in what a High Court judge described as an "extraordinary" and "elaborate campaign of deceit".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The man, who has not been named but was referred to as John in the judgement, applied to the Family Court after he was told the woman had sold their two children for a combined £500.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The case heard that the man received messages and photos of the children and paid the woman around £30,000 over the course of two years.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: But in a hearing in February, the woman, who was referred to as Jane, told the judge she had lied about the pregnancies for revenge, claiming the man had abused her.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The court heard the man believed he was the children's' father because in late 2022 his partner told him she was pregnant, sent pictures of an ultrasound image and had become "visibly pregnant" as time went on.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In May 2023, shortly before the first baby was due, the woman called the police alleging she had been assaulted by the man.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: He was arrested and subsequently held on remand for several months, Mrs Justice Judd said in her ruling which was published on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Following this, the woman sent a message to his stepfather saying the baby had been born as well as sharing baby photos.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: At one stage she is said to have sent voice notes to her former partner's mother in the middle of the night with the sound of a baby crying in the background.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Later, she told the man she was pregnant again and the baby was due in August 2024.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: However, before the due date, the couple split up and did not reconcile.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman would go on to tell the man's mother the baby had been born.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman admitted to the court she had told him she was pregnant when they were together, and afterwards, but conceded she had told a series of elaborate lies and that there were, in fact, no children.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She argued she was menopausal at the time and could not have been pregnant and bank statements show she attended a tanning shop on the day she said she had given birth, Mrs Justice Judd said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In her judgement, the judge concluded that the "factors that weigh against the children genuinely existing were very strong, stronger than the factors pointing the other way".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She said the man was the victim of a "sustained and elaborate campaign of deceit" which also impacted his mother and closest friend.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: "Added to this, the behaviour was cruel, leading a man and his mother to believe they had children and grandchildren respectively.", the Judge said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The judge added she was unable to conclude the woman's motive for her behaviour but said financial fraud was a "possibility"  and that the "complex mental health problems" she suffered from may have also played a part.

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.

sentences.text: Experts warn children as young as five years old are now being groomed on social media and gaming sites Experts are urging parents to talk to their children amid warnings social media grooming is becoming "quicker" and "easier" than ever before.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Childline said Snapchat, TikTok and Instagram were the top platforms children named in counselling about online sexual abuse last year.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The companies have been approached for comment.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Avon and Somerset Police's child exploitation prevention officer Andri Nicolau said children as young as five can be targeted through social media, gaming and messaging platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She urged parents to encourage kids to ask for help without fear of blame or punishment.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The warning comes after three men were jailed for grooming a 17-year-old girl on Snapchat before raping her.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Research by the NSPCC found sexual communication offences involving children in the South West have more than doubled since the offence was introduced seven years ago, to 756 in 2024/25.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Of those, 300 were recorded by Avon and Somerset Police, 96 by Gloucestershire Constabulary and 61 by Wiltshire Police.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The charity also said Snapchat was mentioned in 324 counselling sessions about online sexual abuse between April 2025 and March 2026, a 19% increase on the previous year.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: TikTok (234) and Instagram (197) were the next most frequently mentioned platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Chris Sherwood, chief executive of the NSPCC, said: "It's deeply disturbing that hundreds of children have come to us in the past year alone, disclosing experiences of online sexual abuse linked to these popular apps and platforms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Aqeel used social media, including Snapchat, to arrange to meet young girls.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: He also filmed some of his offences and threatened to share intimate videos and images.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: New data suggests that this particular form of exploitation of children, known as 'sextortion', has also reached record levels.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: The Internet Watch Foundation (IWF) said there has been a sharp rise in the number of young people contacting its confidential Report Remove helpline , external because they fear sexual images of themselves have been shared, or could be shared, online.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Criminals try to extort or blackmail their victims by threatening to publish the images, which have often been taken by the child themselves.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Nicolau said children spending more time online meant they were increasingly vulnerable to grooming, which is "easier" and "quicker" than ever before.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "With online gaming and social media, you have kids from five years old online, some of them have their own phones, so it can be any age," she said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She works with schools to inform children how to be safe online, but said they are often unaware of the risks, including not viewing people they meet online as strangers and expecting them to be "nasty" from the start.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Nicolau encouraged any child or young person who believes they are being groomed to "find someone they are comfortable with and speak to them".
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: She said the police might not be the first choice, but speaking to somebody they trust is what mattered.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Nicolau urged parents to talk to their children and not take away devices or ban them from platforms, warning this could make them feel they were to blame.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Sit down with your child, tell them it's not their fault, even if they've sent indecent images of themselves," she said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Often, particularly if it's to do with grooming or any kind of sexual or romantic relationship, children can be really scared of being judged and embarrassed to talk," said Bradshaw.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Perpetrators are always adapting ways they can better reach young people, whether that's through gaming or social media," he said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: He said another worrying trend was young people turning to AI rather than adults for advice and support about online harms.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Simmons-Read urged parents to normalise conversations with young people about their online lives.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Ella Bradshaw from the NSPCC said children don't speak out because of fear of judgment Ellen Roome, from Cheltenham, who has been campaigning for improvements to online safety since the death of her son Jools in 2022, said not enough is being done to protect young people on social media.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Children are regularly being fed content that is either violent or grooming material and I think as it stands, there isn't any platform that is fully safe for them," she said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "I do think that the social media ban for children will help, but they need to make sure that it is enforced and social media companies are held to account." Ellen Roome has secured rights for families to get social media data from their children's accounts after they pass away.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Simmons-Read said the social media ban for under 16s , which is due to come into force in 2027, "doesn't go far enough", could be bypassed by criminals and could even discourage young people from speaking up about online grooming.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "We want tech platforms to invest more in detecting exploitation when it's happening on their platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: A government spokesperson said it was preparing legislation to make it impossible for children to take, share or view nude images on their devices, which would make the UK the first country to do so.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Alongside this, tech companies must be part of the solution and meet their legal and moral obligations.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Where they fall short, the government will not hesitate to step in," the spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: Kerry Smith, chief executive of the IWF, said: "We welcome the commitment to introducing nudity blocking technology on children's devices – but there really is no time to lose." Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, said it is working to "fight and prevent grooming in a range of ways".
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said: "This includes restricting contact between adults and teens they're not connected to, and using technology to find and remove known child exploitation imagery.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "We also use behavioural signals to identify accounts showing possible signs of grooming or a sexual interest in children.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: "Based on the strength of the signals, we either prevent them from finding and following teens or we remove their account completely." Snapchat and TikTok have all been approached by the BBC for comment.
sentences.article_title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming 'easier'

sentences.text: During the virtual session, pupils asked him about his experiences of living and working in space, as well as the challenges and excitement of space travel.

sentences.text: GE Aerospace previously confirmed fuel got into the river while repair work took place at its site nearby, but NRW said it was working to determine how fuel entered the drainage system and reached the river.
sentences.article_title: Fuel leak which killed fish in River Taff stopped

sentences.text: The Orionid meteor shower, which is capable of producing bright fireball meteors, is set to peak in UK skies in the early hours of Thursday morning.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: Skygazers could spot between 10 and 20 meteors per hour as the celestial spectacle reaches its zenith.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: However clear skies will be needed to see the display and, while some parts of the UK should get a glimpse, cloud and rain may bring frustration in some areas.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: If the weather spoils the view where you are, there will still be chances to see the shower until 7 November.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: The Orionids are an annual meteor shower caused by debris left by Halley's comet in its journey around the Sun.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: Every year, Earth passes through the comet dust and the debris burns with the friction caused by the atmosphere, creating a bright streak of light through the sky.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: The Orionids are fast and bright, entering our atmosphere with speeds of around 41 miles per second.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: They can often produce long glowing trails and fireballs.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: To spot them, find a dark spot with wide open skies, away from city light pollution and let your eyes adjust to the night sky for 20 minutes.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: The meteors are visible to the naked eye so you won't need any specialist equipment like binoculars or a telescope.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: The meteors will appear to originate from the constellation of Orion, near the red supergiant star Betelgeuse.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: This is known as the radiant.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: Between midnight and dawn the constellation will climb higher in the sky to the south and then the south-west.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: It is best to view the meteors slightly away from the radiant as they will be more visible.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: Unfortunately, the Moon will be in the waxing gibbous phase on Wednesday night, throwing extra light into the night sky and reducing visibility.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: However, conditions will improve once the Moon sets around 03:00 BST on Thursday morning.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: Meteor showers are best seen in cloudless skies but these are far from guaranteed.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: Two different weather systems will be affecting the UK during Wednesday night and Thursday morning - one that will bring cloud and rain in north-east Scotland through the early hours, and another that will linger across parts of Wales, the Midlands, East Anglia and south-east England.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: Occasional clear interludes are possible but conditions will generally be challenging for viewing the Orionids in these areas.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: Between these two weather fronts there is a better chance of clear skies overhead - particularly in Northern Ireland, southern Scotland and northern England.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: Clear spells will also develop in south-west England and south Wales but there will be some patchy cloud and a scattering of heavy showers.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: Viewing conditions may remain tricky later in the week, with Storm Austen forecast to bring cloud, rain and gales, and further unsettled weather forecast for the weekend.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: Some fleeting clear spells are always possible and you can keep an eye on the latest forecast for your area here or on the BBC Weather app.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to peak in UK skies into Thursday

sentences.text: Windermere sits at the heart of the iconic Lake District A £3.6bn proposal to stop sewage being discharged into Windermere, England's largest lake, has been unveiled.
sentences.article_title: Giant tunnel proposed to clean up Windermere's sewage problem

sentences.text: The plans, which are backed by the local water company United Utilities and clean water campaigners, would see a tunnel up to 12 miles (19km) long built to transport sewage away from the lake.
sentences.article_title: Giant tunnel proposed to clean up Windermere's sewage problem

sentences.text: At the moment both raw sewage and treated effluent are discharged into Windermere and campaigners say that is why parts of the lake have been turning green each summer, so-called algal blooming.

sentences.text: It is now up to the government to decide if the plan can be further developed, and if the £3.6bn price-tag is acceptable.

sentences.text: That is so big that it can take 9 months for water entering one end to reach the other.

sentences.text: Beardmore said she was excited that a broad coalition including her company, regulators, the local authorities and environmental campaigners had come together to draft this proposal which is called "Only Rainwater into Windermere" (ORiW).

sentences.text: At present the sewage network around Windermere is fragmented, with homes served by a mix of public wastewater treatment works and privately owned treatment facilities and septic tanks.
sentences.article_title: Giant tunnel proposed to clean up Windermere's sewage problem

sentences.text: When treatment works are overwhelmed, such as during heavy rain, they spill raw sewage.
sentences.article_title: Giant tunnel proposed to clean up Windermere's sewage problem

sentences.text: The rest of the time they emit a continuous stream of treated effluent which, while cleaner than raw sewage, can contain high nutrient levels.
sentences.article_title: Giant tunnel proposed to clean up Windermere's sewage problem

sentences.text: On several occasions in the last five years the high nutrient levels and warm temperatures have combined to cause algal blooming turning parts of the lake  a lurid green.
sentences.article_title: Giant tunnel proposed to clean up Windermere's sewage problem

sentences.text: The ORiW proposal would see 12,800 people connected to the sewage network for the first time with up to 86 miles (138km) of new sewage infrastructure and a single wastewater treatment works built to serve them at the end of a 4m-wide sewage tunnel.
sentences.article_title: Giant tunnel proposed to clean up Windermere's sewage problem

sentences.text: Two slightly different plans are being put forward.

sentences.text: Both have the tunnel at their heart but one would see the treated effluent discharged into the River Leven, the other into the Irish Sea at Ulverston.

sentences.article_title: Giant tunnel proposed to clean up Windermere's sewage problem

sentences.text: People like Nigel Wilkinson from Love Windermere group, which is linked to many local businesses, would like the cost to be spread nationally, increasing all bills in England by up to 35p a month.

sentences.text: "We believe Windermere is of such national significance and international significance that it is justifiable to treat this as a national asset and fund it accordingly," he says.

sentences.text: Wildfires have caused thick haze on the streets in Indonesia this month El Niño has been strengthening for several months now and is already having a significant impact on global weather patterns.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Countries including Indonesia, India and the United States have been experiencing droughts, floods and heatwaves in line with projections about how extreme weather events will be supercharged by the phenomenon.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: The World Meteorological Agency says the record-breaking El Niño will strengthen further and persist until at least 2027.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Here are five ways its impact is already being felt around the world.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Several regions around the world are already experiencing anticipated El Niño impacts Indonesia, which typically trends drier and hotter in El Niño years, is battling its worst wildfire season since 2015.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: This year, since January, at least 895,657 hectares of land – nearly six times the size of Greater London – have been burned.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: This is more than twice the area burned last year without the influence of El Niño.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: The wildfires have led to school closures and an increase in hospital admissions across Indonesia.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Millions of people in Sumatra and Kalimantan have been exposed to toxic haze from the fires and around 175,000 people have suffered from respiratory illness.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: More than 40,000 cases – which range from coughs to bronchitis and more serious conditions like pneumonia – involve toddlers.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: In the eastern Pacific, where El Niño tends to strengthen hurricane activity, it has been a very active season so far.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: There have been 22 named storms and 12 hurricanes, including 10 major hurricanes.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: This is already above the number that would typically develop in the whole of an average season, with two months left to go until its end.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Here, El Niño provides the ingredients of higher ocean temperatures and weaker winds high in the atmosphere, making it easier for storms to gain strength.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Hurricane Polo is one such example of this.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: The hurricane experienced rapid intensification, producing wind gusts of 180 mph (285 kmh), fueled by the very warm waters produced by El Niño.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Polo was also one of three hurricanes churning away in the same basin at the same time, along with Odalys and Nolo.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Moreover, it has happened twice now in the space of a month.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Earlier in September, the energy produced by exceptional ocean heat resulted in three simultaneous hurricanes in the central and eastern Pacific: Lowell, Karina and Marie.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Until this year, the last time there had been three Pacific hurricanes at the same time was 2015.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: In contrast, the Atlantic Ocean has remained eerily quiet.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: El Nino has a tendency to increase wind shear in the north Atlantic, a factor which tears apart storms and limits formation.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: There has only been one hurricane - Isaias - which made landfall in the Florida Panhandle and Alabama.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: This was the latest forming hurricane on record in the satellite era (1960s onward).
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Before this year, the record was 11 September, set in 2002 and 2013.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: In an average season, there would have been 10 named storms, five hurricanes and two major hurricanes by this point.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: This year, however, there have only been eight tropical storms: Arthur, Bertha, Cristobal, Dolly, Edouard, Fay, Gonzalo and Hanna.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: The drier and warmer theme has also taken hold in India, where the essential monsoon rainfall has been 13% below average.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: While the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) would consider this still to be in the 'normal' range, the overall average doesn't reflect the variation in rainfall across India.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: While Central India had around its normal expected rainfall, the east and north-east were around 26% drier than average and put into 'exceptional' drought.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Southern states of India were 24% drier than average.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Even where rainfall was nearer to average, the rain did not fall continuously as is typical during the monsoon, instead flipping between long dry spells and extreme rainfall.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: This adds more stress and vulnerability to agriculture yields.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: India is influenced by a number of different weather patterns that can affect the monsoon season and so scientists suggest that El Niño may not have been the only factor.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Further west in the Pacific, it's also been an active season in eastern China and Japan as storms including Maysak and Dujuan have brought recent widespread floods and landslides.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: According to the Japanese Meteorological Agency, there have been 10 tropical cyclones forming in the western Pacific Ocean - the highest number in a season since 1966.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: During El Niño the warmer Pacific brings changes to wind patterns, meaning cyclones tend to form further east, away from Japan and east China.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: However, this means there is a bigger distance and more time where storms can feed off the warmer waters, gaining energy to become more intense typhoons before they hit land.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: Scientists believe that additional typhoons are likely to develop this year with the potential for further impacts to Japan or east China.
sentences.article_title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

sentences.text: "Courage and leadership" are needed to ensure Northern Ireland catches up on tackling climate change.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: The new chair of the Climate Change Committee, Nigel Topping, is spending two days on a fact-finding mission to hear the thoughts of people across different sectors.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: He said Northern Ireland was a small nation that could be "agile and innovative" in tackling challenges like increasing renewable energy, improving waste management and reducing emissions.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: But he warned that a failure to act would mean missing out on innovation opportunities, paying more for energy and damaging the health of children.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: The committee is an independent body advising the UK and devolved governments on emissions targets.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: Over the course of a two-day visit, Topping is meeting farmers, people from the business sector and politicians.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: It is being described as a fact-finding mission, looking at "challenges and opportunities".
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: He acknowledged that politics in Northern Ireland was "complex" and that "when things flip-flop, it doesn't help", due to the impact on investment decisions and people's choices.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: But he said there was "a real sense of collectively wanting to catch up" and avoid anyone being left behind on the road to net zero.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "You've had these lags where there's been no ministers sitting and so there hasn't been policy - there's been civil servants working but no policies," he said.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: Topping said people were experiencing climate change firsthand, with the effects of extreme weather being felt around the UK.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: And he added that that would continue, until emissions reached net zero.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "But I see this as a race between our kind of obstinate, greedy selves and our brilliant, innovative selves," he said.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "And all of us have a bit of both of those extremes and we have those as societies, and I think if we can really tap into backing ourselves as innovators, then we can take this as an opportunity.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "The most important thing for me is that we're going to do this and we're going to have to do this because this is a collective chance for humanity.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "So we can either see it as a burden and complain all of our way and be laggards, or we can see it as an opportunity and say, we're resilient, we're adaptive, we're innovative.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: Nigel Topping is the new chair of the Climate Change Committee When asked what will be the consequences of not taking that "opportunity", he is blunt.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "There's two ways of answering that question.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: One would be, oh, if Northern Ireland doesn't do anything, it doesn't make much difference to the world," he said.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "The other would be, if Northern Ireland doesn't do anything, it misses out on all the innovation opportunities, because other people take those.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "It continues to poison its children's lungs because it doesn't fix the air quality, and it continues to pay more for energy than it needs to.
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "So that's like, dumb, dumb, dumb - why would you do that?
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "So don't get stuck in the we're only small, what difference do we make?
sentences.article_title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change

sentences.text: "But see it as an opportunity as a small nation to be agile and innovative and derive benefit in all those different areas." Climate change scrutiny body to be set up What does the new draft Climate Action Plan mean for NI?

sentences.text: It is the hoped the lab will become a hub for upland research A new, purpose-built laboratory will serve as a base for scientists, universities and students to investigate Cumbria's upland landscapes, and how they respond to nature recovery.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: It is hoped the research facility at RSPB Wild Haweswater, in Penrith, will become a hub for upland science, bringing researchers and conservationists together to carry out fieldwork, share expertise, and develop new collaborations.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: The lab was funded by the estate of the late ornithologist Denis Summers-Smith.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: "We want to build on Denis's commitment to field ecology and conservation research, creating a lasting legacy that will benefit both science and nature recovery in Cumbria and beyond," said RSPB's Will Peach.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: The new lab will support current research through Cumbria Connect, whose work and scientific monitoring spans Wild Haweswater, the Lowther estate and the Lowther Valley.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: Dr Mo Verhoeven, conservation scientist at Cumbria Connect, explained how the region's landscape is made up of a number of distinctive environments, including peatlands and rainforest, which play a key role in storing carbon and managing water.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: "Cumbria's uplands are incredibly important for nature recovery," he said.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: "We hope this laboratory will give researchers, students and conservationists a place to work together and build the evidence needed to guide restoration, both here in Cumbria and in upland landscapes further afield.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: "It's about making Cumbria a much stronger base for upland science." "Just as importantly, it will help train the next generation of environmental scientists," he said.
sentences.article_title: New lab to become centre for investigating uplands

sentences.text: Cumbria Connect is part of a scheme paid for by the Arcadia Fund which was co-founded by one of the heirs to the Tetra Pak fortune.

sentences.text: A Saudi national charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's meeting rooms has been accused of having "considerable support" from the Saudi government, according to a court filing , external in California.
